messages:
anya: Quick sync — I'm proposing an explicit operator grace period + staged-apply backpressure model for on‑prem package activation. Main goals: avoid long operator lockouts, make rollbacks safe, and bound resource spikes during mass-activations.
kevin: +1 on the goals. can you sketch the lifecycle? curious how this interacts with seed transfer and verifier handshakes.
mike: We should be careful about timing windows — some airgapped sites have slow flash. If grace is too short, operators will retry and cause thundering herd.
sara: Also how do we surface progress to customers? ops teams want a simple status and ETA, not a wall of logs.
anya: Sketch: 1) operator enters PREP state on manifest apply; 2) operator reserves activation window (epoch token) but doesn't stream blobs; 3) verifier handshake occurs; 4) staged-apply phases with configurable concurrency and a soft/hard grace period; 5) commit or rollback. Backpressure is applied during stage boundaries to limit concurrent blob apply and CPU/memory pressure.
kevin: Nice. What enforces backpressure? kube operator throttle? agent-side token bucket?
anya: Plan is hybrid: controller grants an activation lease (count + weight) per node group. Agents take tokens before starting heavy extraction. Controller reduces grant when cluster memory pressure or IO errors exceed thresholds. Pseudoconfig: ```activation: grace_soft: 10m grace_hard: 2h concurrency: 3 per-node weight: 1e6 backpressure: { io_threshold: 70, mem_threshold: 80 }```
mike: That config looks reasonable. One risk: if controller loses quorum while a stage is mid-apply, do we auto-fail-safe? We need idempotent apply markers on disk.
anya: Yes — every stage writes a local apply marker and a checkpoint manifest (sha256). If controller is unreachable, agents continue limited apply with last-known tokens until grace_hard. After that they pause and emit an operator-alert.
sara: For UI/observability, can we surface per-node stage + estimated remaining bytes? Even a rough ETA is better. devex-bot can add a small UI card.
devex-bot: @sara noted. I can add a per-route telemetry card with bytes-applied/total and current-stage. Will need a light-weight websocket for streaming progress.
kevin: About rollbacks: do we allow cross-node partial rollback? e.g., some nodes committed, others didn't.
anya: We enforce activation epochs — commit is all-or-nothing from the control plane perspective. If any subset fails commit constraints, operator transitions to SAFE-ROLLBACK and we run a two-phase rollback with staged revert. Agents keep tombstone markers so the rollback is deterministic.
mike: Two questions: 1) how do we test this at scale in CI? 2) what recovery playbook for powercuts mid-stage?
anya: 1) CI: synthetic slow-storage sim, random IO faults, and chaos testing on seed transfer. We'll run canary clusters with reduced concurrency to validate. 2) Recovery: agent on restart replays checkpoint manifests; if marker present, resume/rollback depending on last control directive. We'll include a dry-run apply mode for operator to pre-check.
sara: Operators will ask "how long will this take" — can we provide a conservative estimate: bytes / min_io_rate * safety_factor?
mike: Yes, but require per-node profiling. Maybe initial bootstrap uses historical throughput, then adjust with exponential smoothing.
kevin: Minor: add a breaker that switches to offloading mode — i.e., pause activation and instead move to staggered fetch via operator-managed staging buckets (USB/airgap media). Useful for really constrained sites.
anya: Good idea. Add fallback path flag: offline_staging: true -> switch to manual-stage workflow with admin acknowledgement.
kevin: Ok. I'm mostly worried about complexity. We should aim to keep the default behavior simple: single token, short soft grace, automatic backpressure, telemetry. Advanced options tucked behind flags.
sara: Agreed. Can we capture this as a short RFC PR? I'll volunteer to write the operator UX section.
anya: I'll open the RFC branch with the lifecycle diagram and config schema. @kevin can you add the controller token semantics? @mike can you draft the idempotent marker format (on-disk) and resume rules?
kevin: Yep, will do.
mike: I'll draft the markers with examples: /var/lib/redwood/activation/<epoch>.marker -> {status: staging|committed|rollback, sha256:..., applied_bytes:...} and include a small recovery-state machine.
ops-bot: deployment started: rfc/airgap-operator-grace-389 by anya (draft). reviewers: kevin, mike, sara.
anya: Thanks. I'll ping eng-sre and support for playbook feedback. Short sync tomorrow 10:30 PT?
sara: Works for me. :thumbsup:
kevin: Works.
mike: Works.
anya: Great — RFC incoming.
